title: Variance-Reduced Forward-Reflected-Backward Splitting Methods for Nonmonotone Generalized Equations

source_version.publication: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR volume 267 (2025)
source_version.version_basis: official publisher linked PDF acquired on retrieval date, frozen by SHA-256

inspection_outcome: Demonstrated core quantitative and derivational errors with verified restricted repairs; two local application mapping defects; empirical claims remain source-bounded
summary: Theorem4.1 displacement bound is false on an admissible scalar instance and initial potential calculation drops a positive term. SAGA's unrestricted specified recurrence and Cor3.3 eta lower bound fail; a dependence-safe recurrence proof restores the core batch regime. A2's advertised nonmonotone example violates assumptions. Generic convergence order and empirical ranking are not declared false.

focused_acceptance.assumptions_and_decisive_evidence: The admissible zero-G, T=(8/3)I example with gamma=3/4, eta=1/2, x0=1/100 and y0=1/50 satisfies the stated operator and initialization conditions. It gives x1=1/120, Rhat0^2=1/5000, displacement LHS=1/720000>RHS=1/1093750. The initial potential is 21/50000>2 Rhat0^2=1/2500, exposing the dropped positive term.
focused_acceptance.counterevidence_and_limits: The corrected (2+mu) Rhat0^2 initial estimate can repair constants. It does not make the printed quartic scaling or original initial-potential inequality true.
focused_acceptance.core_dependency_and_severity: Major is retained for a false bound within the core convergence theorem, without requiring divergence or a performance loss.
focused_acceptance.correction_scope: The report propagates the corrected initial factor locally and keeps full-history conditioning and strict step-size assumptions; no unrestricted global repair is claimed.

focused_acceptance.assumptions_and_decisive_evidence: Same-batch dependence invalidates the printed SAGA factorization. The legal n=2,b=1 VFR example gives Delta2=4041/4096000 versus factorized 1611/1638400, a difference 27/8192000. The separate generic adapted n=20,b=19 example violates the unrestricted lemma recurrence by 9943/571824000. For n=1000,b=100 the checked step bound is sqrt(1200/54913)=0.14782675<0.1494.
focused_acceptance.counterevidence_and_limits: The legal VFR example still satisfies its recurrence bound; the generic counterexample is not a VFR trajectory and is outside the main corollary batch range. The dependence-safe PSD repair covers b<=n^(2/3), preserving a restricted complexity-order result.
focused_acceptance.core_dependency_and_severity: Major is retained for the invalid conditioning and stated core estimator/step-size guarantees, while explicitly preserving the narrower results actually supported.
focused_acceptance.correction_scope: The d+I(r-gamma s) decomposition and restricted PSD correction are retained with their conditions; the report does not infer general divergence, and its corrected residual bound remains below 526.

problems.title: Ineligible advertised nonmonotone example
problems.outcome: Demonstrated invalid core-scope illustrative derivation; alternative example verified
problems.claim: A2 claimsGPSD,Teligible and weakMinty withkappa=epsilon forarbitrarilysmallepsilon

focused_acceptance.assumptions_and_decisive_evidence: The advertised example has G eigenvalues +/-1 rather than being positive semidefinite, and its T is not monotone. The weak-Minty matrix determinant is 2 epsilon^2-1; epsilon=0.01 and direction (1,-1) fail the claimed inequality.
focused_acceptance.counterevidence_and_limits: This ineligible example is not an admissible counterexample to the abstract theorem. The report's skew-plus-negative-scalar replacement satisfies the intended conditions and shows the broader phenomenon is possible.
focused_acceptance.core_dependency_and_severity: Major is retained because the introduction expressly invokes this example to substantiate the core nonmonotone coverage claim; repairability and appendix location do not erase that invalid derivation.
focused_acceptance.correction_scope: The replacement example repairs that illustration only and is not presented as a repair of all theorem constants or experiments.

problems.title: Quadratic objective-to-operator mapping differs
problems.outcome: Demonstrated local mathematical mapping defect; historicaleffectNeedsEvidence

focused_acceptance.assumptions_and_decisive_evidence: Differentiating the stated quadratic saddle objective yields blocks [2A,L;-L^T,2B], with the transpose required for rectangular L. The checked scalar root of the printed operator is not stationary for the stated objective.
focused_acceptance.counterevidence_and_limits: The alternative printed operator can still define a test inclusion for the general solver. The demonstrated mismatch does not by itself invalidate the abstract solver guarantee or its main comparison.
focused_acceptance.core_dependency_and_severity: Minor is retained on this specific application-mapping dependency, not on a requirement for historical benchmark loss.
focused_acceptance.correction_scope: The corrected objective-to-operator map is given analytically; the report does not claim that historical numerical experiments used it.

problems.title: Robust logistic reformulation switches uncertainty model

focused_acceptance.assumptions_and_decisive_evidence: The source exchanges a sum of observation-specific maxima for one shared simplex variable. The two opposed scalar logistic observations yield a gap of exactly 1, disproving that equality.
focused_acceptance.counterevidence_and_limits: Independent z_i variables restore the per-observation model; alternatively, one shared z defines a different coherent uncertainty model. Either can still serve as a solver application.
focused_acceptance.core_dependency_and_severity: Minor is retained for the bounded application-model equivalence error rather than a disproof of the core solver theorem.
focused_acceptance.correction_scope: The report states the two distinct valid formulations and does not conflate their repaired experiments or scores.

problems.title: Experimental nonmonotonicity and oracle cost need binding

focused_acceptance.assumptions_and_decisive_evidence: Indefinite components do not ensure an indefinite average, and the reported instances do not provide the spectra/weak-Minty constants needed to bind the claimed experimental regime. Epoch counts also need component-call and residual-parameter conventions for like-for-like oracle comparison.
focused_acceptance.counterevidence_and_limits: The paper discloses ten-instance averages, manual/larger step choices, and exclusion of unstable baselines. These disclosures are preserved and do not prove manipulation or an actual ranking reversal.
focused_acceptance.core_dependency_and_severity: Needs Evidence is retained for missing instance/assumption/cost bindings; no additional established core performance failure is inferred.
focused_acceptance.correction_scope: Exact instances, constants, and oracle accounting are the unresolved items; no duplicate experiment or corrected ranking is claimed.
